From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

## Executive view

The Seller’s package departs materially from the Buyer playbook. The main issues are the proposed reduction and expansion of the liability limitations, inadequate treatment of title and fundamental warranties, blanket deemed disclosure and Buyer-knowledge exclusions, and unresolved Completion risks concerning Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses and Ironquay.

Several statements in the Seller Update—such as “agreed price mechanics”, “addressed”, “adequate” and “settled”—are Seller assertions, not evidence of agreement or internal authority. In particular, neither the 20% cap nor the 18-month period is authorised merely because each matches a possible fallback.

## Detailed review and pushback

### 1. General Warranty cap

**Seller position:** 20% of price—AUD 4.8 million.

**Departure:** Our opening and currently authorised position is 25%—AUD 6 million. A 20% cap is available only with Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying the relevant draft. No approval has been given.

**Pushback:**

- Restore the General Warranty cap to **AUD 6 million / 25%**.
- Make clear it applies only to General Warranty Claims, not title, tax, specific indemnities, payment obligations, covenants or fraud-related claims.
- Do not treat the numerical 20% fallback as cleared.

### 2. De minimis and basket

**Seller position:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; only loss above the basket is recoverable.

**Departure:** The playbook requires:

- AUD 5,000 de minimis;
- AUD 50,000 aggregate basket; and
- a **tipping basket**, so the Seller is liable from the first dollar of qualifying claims once the basket is exceeded.

The Seller proposal is five times higher at both levels and converts the basket into a deductible.

**Pushback:** Reinstate the Buyer thresholds and first-dollar recovery. The drafting should also prevent related claims or a series arising from the same facts from being artificially split for de minimis purposes.

### 3. General claims period

**Seller position:** 18 months after Completion, with limitations presumptively applying to all Claims.

**Departure:** Our authorised position is 24 months. Eighteen months requires prior written Amelia Frost approval, which has not been given. The proposed catch-all application to “all Claims” also risks overriding the separate regimes required by the playbook.

**Pushback:**

- Restore **24 months** for General Warranty Claims.
- Delete the presumption that a limitation applies to all Claims unless excluded.
- State affirmatively that the general regime applies only to General Warranty Claims.
- Preserve properly notified, contingent or unquantified claims without requiring final quantification before expiry.

### 4. Fundamental, title, capacity and authority claims

**Seller position:** Same caps and periods as General Warranties “for administrative simplicity”.

**Departure:** This is fundamentally inconsistent with the playbook. Title and fundamental claims require:

- a 100% purchase-price cap;
- at least six years;
- no general de minimis or basket; and
- no Buyer-knowledge bar.

“Administrative simplicity” does not justify transferring ownership risk to the Buyer.

**Pushback:** Create an express separate regime for title, ownership, capacity and authority warranties, with a **100% cap and minimum six-year period**, outside the general thresholds and knowledge limitations.

### 5. Fraud and deliberate wrongdoing

**Seller position:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

**Departure:** The playbook requires fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct to be carved out of every:

- cap;
- threshold or basket;
- time limit;
- exclusive-remedy clause; and
- non-reliance provision,

to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-waivable.

**Pushback:** Insert an overriding, consistently defined carve-out in every relevant provision. It should not be defeated by characterising a claim as contractual, tortious, statutory or otherwise.

### 6. Other claims must not be swept into the general regime

The Seller’s proposed “all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise” structure creates a serious hidden-allocation risk.

**Pushback:** Keep separate regimes for:

- General Warranties;
- title, ownership, capacity and authority;
- tax;
- IP and specific indemnities;
- purchase-price and payment obligations;
- Completion and post-Completion covenants; and
- fraud and deliberate wrongdoing.

Each limitation should apply only where expressly identified. Tax and IP remain open; the Seller’s statement that they are “settled” has no effect. We should not assume either unlimited liability or acceptance of the general cap.

### 7. Disclosure standard

**Seller position:** General disclosure of the whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records.

**Departure:** This conflicts with the required specific fair-disclosure standard. It would force the Buyer to construct exceptions from a large body of material and, together with the knowledge clause, could eliminate claims for matters merely discoverable somewhere in due diligence.

**Pushback:**

- Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 as general deemed disclosure.
- Require each exception to be **specifically and fairly disclosed**, in sufficient detail to identify its nature, scope and reasonably apparent consequences.
- Require each disclosure to identify the particular warranty or warranties it qualifies.
- Reject deemed disclosure through public registers, prudent searches, the general data room or mere references to documents.
- Require an updated disclosure letter and refreshed index at signing, and a controlled update/bring-down process before Completion. The present letter refers to a data-room cutoff of **22 September 2026**, so its currency should be verified.

The “no admission” reservation can remain as procedural wording only if it does not dilute the agreed disclosure standard or risk allocation.

### 8. Buyer knowledge

**Seller position:** No claim for anything known by the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records.

**Departure:** This is much broader than actual knowledge. It imputes adviser knowledge and constructive knowledge and effectively duplicates the proposed general disclosure.

**Pushback:**

- Delete the blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusion.
- Reject “discoverable”, constructive, imputed adviser and public-record knowledge.
- Any knowledge qualification in the warranties should instead be tightly framed by reference to named Seller knowledge persons who have made reasonable enquiry.
- In all events, knowledge must not excuse title, ownership, capacity, authority, fraud or specific-indemnity liability.

### 9. Bluefen consent

**Facts disclosed:** Bluefen accounts for approximately AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue, around 30%. No final written consent or evidence that its conditions have been satisfied is included.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent.

**Departure:** This is not sufficient for a material customer. Delivery does not establish that the consent is effective or that clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.

**Pushback:** Retain as a substantive condition precedent requiring before Completion:

- effective written consent;
- compliance with or satisfaction of all conditions to that consent;
- evidence reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer; and
- no adverse amendment, waiver, termination right, price change or other material condition unless accepted by the Buyer.

Reasonable endeavours alone is not an acceptable substitute.

### 10. Riverlark facility and security releases

**Facts disclosed:** Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding; the facility is unpaid and no final discharge is available.

**Seller position:** Release after Completion.

**Departure:** This is incompatible with the debt-free/cash-free acquisition structure and leaves the Buyer exposed to existing security after it has paid the price.

**Pushback:** Require:

- a current lender payout statement;
- direct payment to Riverlark from Completion funds;
- simultaneous effective releases of all Company security, guarantees and related claims; and
- evidence of discharge and any necessary register-release steps.

A post-Completion release is not acceptable unless supported by an irrevocable lender undertaking and specifically approved by Amelia Frost. No such approval exists. “Approximately” AUD 3.2 million is not adequate for final funds flow.

### 11. Employee Completion bonuses

**Facts disclosed:** DD-005 records AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses; they are omitted from the funds flow, and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unresolved.

**Seller position:** A Seller matter, but not separately itemised.

**Problem:** If these liabilities are triggered by the transaction but remain payable by the Company after Completion, the Buyer may economically fund them despite the stated position.

**Pushback:**

- Quantify the AUD 420,000 plus all applicable on-costs.
- Include the amount expressly in the Completion funds flow, or require it to be fully Seller-funded.
- Specify payment, withholding, payroll-tax and superannuation mechanics.
- Ensure there is no double counting through debt, working capital or another adjustment.
- Obtain a Completion confirmation of the recipients, conditions and amounts.

### 12. Ironquay IP

**Facts disclosed:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but that amount and non-payment have not been independently verified. There is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.

**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment.

**Departure:** A payment-only indemnity may not protect the Buyer if the real issue is ownership, transfer, licensing, infringement, incomplete deliverables or failure of the cure mechanics.

**Pushback:**

- Preserve the contractual SOW3 cure.
- Obtain independent confirmation of the amount owing, direct evidence of cleared payment and an effective assignment/confirmation from Ironquay.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover losses arising from failure to obtain valid ownership or the necessary rights in the Project Materials, including associated payment, infringement and remediation exposure.
- Keep the specific IP indemnity separate from the General Warranty regime.
- Do not accept AUD 180,000 as established in either direction until verified.

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident

**Facts disclosed:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address and may concern approximately 1,240 records. Access, scope, notification requirements, breach status and loss remain unconfirmed.

**Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Assessment:** “Not expected to be material” is unsupported. Equally, the present material does not justify asserting a confirmed breach, notification duty, harm or monetary demand.

**Pushback:** Require pre-Completion obligations to:

- preserve all relevant logs, emails, system records and evidence;
- continue a properly scoped investigation;
- provide prompt written updates and underlying findings;
- establish whether the link was accessed, downloaded, forwarded or disabled;
- assess applicable privacy, contractual and regulatory duties; and
- consult with the Buyer before notifications or admissions, subject to legal requirements.

Include cooperation, remediation and document-preservation obligations after Completion. Final allocation, including whether a specific indemnity is needed, should follow verified findings rather than the Seller’s materiality assertion.

### 14. Sandbar supplier renewals

**Facts disclosed:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, totalling AUD 330,000. The disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Assessment:** That conclusion is not supported by the disclosure itself. However, the amount should not automatically be classified as Debt or deducted from price.

**Pushback:** Review the underlying contracts, renewal timing, termination rights, service periods, accrual treatment and consistency with past practice. Then determine the correct working-capital, ordinary-course or specific-adjustment treatment. Do not permit silent treatment in the price mechanics.

### 15. Title evidence

**Seller position:** DD-012 share register proves title to 100% of the shares.

**Departure:** DD-012 is a supplied internal Company record, not independent proof of ownership, absence of encumbrances or Seller authority.

**Pushback:** Require corroborating evidence, including as applicable:

- share certificates and transfer history;
- constitution and relevant corporate approvals;
- Seller authority and execution approvals;
- searches for security interests or encumbrances;
- confirmation of issued capital, options and other rights;
- evidence that no beneficial, trust, nominee or third-party interests exist; and
- delivery of valid transfers and title documents at Completion.

The title warranties and 100% liability regime remain necessary regardless of diligence.

### 16. Office lease and Mossvale

The disclosures do not establish that either landlord or Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold. We should not accept an unnecessary consent condition based only on the Seller’s references.

Nevertheless:

- verify and comply with any office-lease notification obligation; and
- review the Mossvale assignment and any change-of-control language in the full contract.

Any disclosure should qualify only the specifically relevant warranty and should not create a general knowledge bar.

## Recommended negotiation position

1. Restore the **25% / AUD 6 million** General Warranty cap.
2. Reinstate the **AUD 5,000 de minimis**, **AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, and first-dollar recovery.
3. Restore the **24-month** general claims period.
4. Create a separate **100% / at least six-year** regime for title, ownership, capacity and authority.
5. Add overriding fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate-misconduct carve-outs.
6. Reject the general “all Claims” limitation structure and keep each liability category separate.
7. Delete whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search disclosure.
8. Delete the blanket Buyer/adviser knowledge exclusion.
9. Make effective Bluefen consent and satisfaction of its conditions a genuine Completion condition.
10. Require Riverlark repayment directly from Completion funds and simultaneous effective security releases.
11. Expressly fund or itemise the AUD 420,000 bonuses and all on-costs.
12. Verify and broaden the Ironquay protection while preserving the SOW3 cure.
13. Impose evidence-preservation, investigation and update obligations for DD-006 without assuming a breach or loss.
14. Investigate Sandbar before assigning price-mechanics treatment.
15. Require independent title and authority evidence beyond DD-012.
16. Treat tax and IP as still open and reject any suggestion that the Seller has unilaterally settled them under the general regime.

- Obtain independent confirmation of the amount owing, direct evidence of cleared payment and an effective assignment/confirmation from Ironquay.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover losses arising from failure to obtain valid ownership or the necessary rights in the Project Materials, including associated payment, infringement and remediation exposure.
- Keep the specific IP indemnity separate from the General Warranty regime.
- Do not accept AUD 180,000 as established in either direction until verified.

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident

**Facts disclosed:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address and may concern approximately 1,240 records. Access, scope, notification requirements, breach status and loss remain unconfirmed.

**Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Assessment:** “Not expected to be material” is unsupported. Equally, the present material does not justify asserting a confirmed breach, notification duty, harm or monetary demand.

**Pushback:** Require pre-Completion obligations to:

- preserve all relevant logs, emails, system records and evidence;
- continue a properly scoped investigation;
- provide prompt written updates and underlying findings;
- establish whether the link was accessed, downloaded, forwarded or disabled;
- assess applicable privacy, contractual and regulatory duties; and
- consult with the Buyer before notifications or admissions, subject to legal requirements.

Include cooperation, remediation and document-preservation obligations after Completion. Final allocation, including whether a specific indemnity is needed, should follow verified findings rather than the Seller’s materiality assertion.

### 14. Sandbar supplier renewals

**Facts disclosed:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, totalling AUD 330,000. The disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Assessment:** That conclusion is not supported by the disclosure itself. However, the amount should not automatically be classified as Debt or deducted from price.

**Pushback:** Review the underlying contracts, renewal timing, termination rights, service periods, accrual treatment and consistency with past practice. Then determine the correct working-capital, ordinary-course or specific-adjustment treatment. Do not permit silent treatment in the price mechanics.

### 15. Title evidence

**Seller position:** DD-012 share register proves title to 100% of the shares.

**Departure:** DD-012 is a supplied internal Company record, not independent proof of ownership, absence of encumbrances or Seller authority.

**Pushback:** Require corroborating evidence, including as applicable:

- share certificates and transfer history;
- constitution and relevant corporate approvals;
- Seller authority and execution approvals;
- searches for security interests or encumbrances;
- confirmation of issued capital, options and other rights;
- evidence that no beneficial, trust, nominee or third-party interests exist; and
- delivery of valid transfers and title documents at Completion.

The title warranties and 100% liability regime remain necessary regardless of diligence.

### 16. Office lease and Mossvale

The disclosures do not establish that either landlord or Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold. We should not accept an unnecessary consent condition based only on the Seller’s references.

Nevertheless:

- verify and comply with any office-lease notification obligation; and
- review the Mossvale assignment and any change-of-control language in the full contract.

Any disclosure should qualify only the specifically relevant warranty and should not create a general knowledge bar.

1. Restore the **25% / AUD 6 million** General Warranty cap.
2. Reinstate the **AUD 5,000 de minimis**, **AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, and first-dollar recovery.
3. Restore the **24-month** general claims period.
4. Create a separate **100% / at least six-year** regime for title, ownership, capacity and authority.
5. Add overriding fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate-misconduct carve-outs.
6. Reject the general “all Claims” limitation structure and keep each liability category separate.
7. Delete whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search disclosure.
8. Delete the blanket Buyer/adviser knowledge exclusion.
9. Make effective Bluefen consent and satisfaction of its conditions a genuine Completion condition.
10. Require Riverlark repayment directly from Completion funds and simultaneous effective security releases.
11. Expressly fund or itemise the AUD 420,000 bonuses and all on-costs.
12. Verify and broaden the Ironquay protection while preserving the SOW3 cure.
13. Impose evidence-preservation, investigation and update obligations for DD-006 without assuming a breach or loss.
14. Investigate Sandbar before assigning price-mechanics treatment.
